utterances.text: I think that is correct, and the translations have now been provided. And the Chamber is about to give a decision whether these may be added to the 65 ter list or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01189 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we move now to 5313.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This relates to the personnel who had already been on the mission and who are returning from assignment that they should be allowed some free days upon this assignment completion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: A problem is providing a B/C/S image of this document. We have only English apparently in e-court, the reverse of earlier problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could I, with the assistance of the Usher, hand to the witness a B/C/S copy. And we could also sort out the e-court issue in the break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This dispatch number 436 of March 2, 1999 --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Deals with the deployment --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm just reminded, Your Honours, that this document -- we removed it from e-court this morning because it's a duplicate of another document that we'll be seeing. I'm so sorry. Please accept my apologies, Your Honours. If I could move on to 5314. And this is the 9th of March, 1999, shortly before the hostilities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The dispatch relating to the deployment of Special Police Units to Kosovo and Metohija from other Secretariats, from Nis, Pirot, Krusevac, Prokuplje, Leskovac and Vranje. And it is from the public security department, we see this on the first page. And the Uzice Secretariat is not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you see who signed it, who in particular it's from?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: I can't see the second page. It was signed by the chief of the public security sector, Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, could 5314 be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01190.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in this batch, Mr. Keric, the last one I'd like to look at is 4095, which is P346 already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This relates to a rotation of units. And we see the number of men who were sent from various Secretariats, including Uzice, as we can see here, from the 35th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could go to the last page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's something -- there's a problem here. I can't see what this is about. I don't see a signature. There is some signature, but I don't see the signature of the undersigned. This is a standard dispatch, but I can't see the signature of the sender. There's only a facsimile.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. In the version you have in Serbian, is this a telefaxed copy or the telegraphed copy?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: The copy in the Serbian language is a fax or a telefax copy of the dispatch. There is no signature, handwritten signature. There is a signature just typed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, you indicated that it is a standard dispatch. And I think you recall that in most of them - in all of them that we have looked at from the first one shown to you today from 11th of December, 1998, to this one, immediately before the hostilities - they came from the assistant minister in charge of the public security department. In the last paragraph we also see here, and this is also very standards in the dispatches: "Ministry PJP command is to be informed by dispatch at the time of departure, march route, number of employees and vehicles and employees who have not gone on this assignment, including the reasons for their absence." So do you recall that after the units were deployed, the SUP chiefs had the responsibility to inform the PJP command of these matters described in this last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: In each of these cases, the chiefs of Secretariats were duty-bound to inform the command of the Special Police Unit of the number of men that they are sending and the number of men who did not go on assignment for reasons of their own or otherwise. And -- because some people just refused to go. And they had to inform the PJP command thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like us to move on to look at some of the documents in which the chiefs of the SUPs would inform whether they will comply.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we first look at 05264. Well, before we move from this document, before we move on, can we just go back to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I just want you to note here, Mr. Keric, that this is dispatch number 587 on the 21st of March. Do you observe that?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, if we could move on to 65 ter number 5264.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you tell us briefly who this is from and what this purports to accomplish?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: This is information in response to Dispatch 587 from the public security department which ordered the deployment. And this information is to inform them how many men have been sent, how many were absent, and for what reasons. And as we can see, there's also mention of the route they took, and this route actually corresponds to what was ordered in that dispatch. Basically, they are just reporting that they had followed the instructions or orders as issued earlier by the chief of this department.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, and this is one that you sent yourself?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: No, it was our duty to do so, as I mentioned earlier. In each instance where a certain number of men are ordered to be sent to Kosovo and Metohija, we had the duty to report whether all the men who had been mentioned in the dispatch of the chief of the department had been sent and who had not been sent, and practically this is just in response to the order sending these men.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. I just asked if this one, this response, is your response?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes. This is my reply. Actually, the reply from the Secretariat in Uzice. But whether I actually signed this or the chief of the crime police because he coordinated all this, so on some occasions he would sign these dispatches that had to do with assigning of men to a certain task or a mission because this was part of the work that was to be done by the Secretariat in Uzice. But at times, I would get a dispatch to sign of this type. In this particular case I can't see whether I actually did sign it or whether it was signed by the chief of the department who was acting at the time. I can't see here exactly, it doesn't state clearly whether I actually signed this or not, but most probably I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And bearing in mind the last order, the previous order we saw from General Djordjevic deploying PJP units to Kosovo, you note here that the subject line indicates that this is in regard to RJB dispatch number 587 on the 21st of March, 1999, which is the same dispatch number and date of that last dispatch that we looked at.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: If you read this carefully, you can see that it says: "Reference to ..." In other words, we are referring to dispatch 587 of 21st March, and this was done, it was accomplished on the 21st or 22nd of March, on that night. And then on the next day we prepared the reply saying that all the measures as ordered by this dispatch were actually implemented. So this is in reference to dispatch number 587.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if you look above that, we see the addressees. Was it addressed to the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, the police administration, and the PJP command?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: It was addressed to the Ministry of the Interior, the police administration, in other words, the uniformed police, and also to the PJP or Special Police Unit command. I think, I'm not sure, but there may have been other replies from the Uzice Secretariat or from other parts of Serbia, but in any case, these replies were sent to the police administration or to the PJP command. So these orders, dispatches containing orders, were signed by the chief of the public security; but the replies were sent to the PJP command and the police administration because the PJP command probably was part of the police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But I see also the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. Was it also sent to the MUP or the seat of the MUP headquarters in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: The seat of the MUP headquarters in Belgrade, yes, precisely. All dispatches were sent to the ministry, and particulars are given at the bottom of the dispatch, or below it to whom it was sent. Whether it was the police administration or the traffic administration or the border police, and so on. This was standard procedure, and I think it was done the same way in all other Secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Organisationally in the MUP, who or what bodies were the police administration and the PJP command subordinate to?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: The police administration and the PJP command, I know for certain that the police administration was subordinated to the public security department. The command of the PJP, I think I've already mentioned this, I think was in a special status. Formally it was within the police administration. However, I think that it was at a higher level and that it had closer ties with the minister rather than the police administration. And the police administration also had certain tasks regarding the training, equipment, logistics of those units that were used by the PJP units of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Your Honours, could this document be given an --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01191.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I think, Your Honours, this is also another one that is not yet on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P01191 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll have our second break now, resuming at 5 minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Keric, you said in the last session that there were similar orders or similar responses like the one you sent back to the MUP headquarters in respect to the dispatch you had gotten from the MUP headquarters, number 587, you say that other SUPs would have sent back the same or a similar response indicating the level of compliance in their area. And I'd like to show you some of those very quickly and for you to tell us if these are documents that you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at 5262, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the same text as before. It's a response that people were sent out to mission, but it's very specific here. It says Republic of Serbia MUP, and it's only for PJPs. As I said, PJPs, Special Police Units, were formally part of the police administration, but organisationally and all other issues concerning the equipment and vehicles were handled, in my opinion, by the minister rather than any other organisational part. In this particular document, it's only sent to the PJP, the response, in this case. And it's signed by the police department chief, and it's related to your question on whether I signed the fax. Sometimes I signed it if the police department chief brought it to me, or it could have been signed only by the police department chief, which was done in this particular case. It says it was signed by the Lieutenant-Colonel Miloslav Dimitrijevic. So it was head of the Secretariat, chief of the Secretariat, but chief of the police department. I don't know if I'm clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could this one be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01192.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. And this one is similar, I'm now informed, Your Honour, to the others that are not yet on the list but for which applications were made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As you indicated, Mr. Stamp, it appears that it must be marked at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So, Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01192 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could look at 5262. Sorry, 5263.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that a similar dispatch or a response from the SUP Subotica this time to --

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: This document is completely identical to the previous one, apart from the fact that in this case, unlike the case of Smederevo, this is sent to the police administration and the PJP command. And it is signed also by the chief of the police department and not by the chief of the Secretariat, because these tasks of informing people and sending out people were under the direct authorities of the police department, or rather, the chief of the police department.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Could this one also be marked for identity, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01193 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we now look at 5265.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that a similar response from the SUP Prokuplje?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: The answer is the same as before, but in this case, this document was sent only to the PJP command. And it was, again, signed by the chief of the police department and not by the chief of the Secretariat, which is in line with what I've previously said. And it's sent to the police department too, sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could this also be marked for identity, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01194 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we now look at 5266.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is also the same response to the dispatch. It was sent only to the PJP command, not the police administration, and it was signed by the chief of the department from Kikinda.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could this be marked as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01195 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we bring up 5270.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the same substance of the document. It is sent to the police administration and PJP command, and it was signed by the chief of the Secretariat in Pancevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could this be given an -- or could this be marked for identity, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01196 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at 5271.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is also a response to the dispatch for staff from Pirot to be sent out. Only the chief of the Pirot SUP signed it. And I think in 1999, the chief of the police administration was Mr. Simic, but the chief of the Secretariat signed it from Pirot.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could this also be marked for identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01197 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we see 5273.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you just move the document to the part where I can see the signature, please. This is addressed to the police administration, and it was signed by the chief of the Secretariat at that time Major-General Marinko Kresoja the substance is the same for the deployment of personnel in the area of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could that one also be marked for identity, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01198 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And could we now look at 5274.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is from Sombor addressed to the police administration and the PJP command, signed by, just a minute, chief -- it doesn't say of what. I suppose it's the chief of SUP, should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could that one be given an exhibit number -- sorry, could be marked for identity as well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01199 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And could we look at 5261.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This one -- well, could you tell us what this one is about? You know the date and that in the reference section it is --

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: It's the same dispatch from 1998. It's a response to dispatch. It provides information on what was done upon the order or the dispatch from 17th of July, 1175, which means of transport shall be used, and which routes. Chief of Secretariat is to be signed -- it was either signed by me or the chief of police department. In other Secretariats it was the chiefs of police departments who signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So can I take it from these responses, showing compliance with the order of the assistant minister in charge of the RJB General Djordjevic, that the system remained the same between 1998 and 1999 in terms of how units were deployed in Kosovo and the responsibility to report as to compliance with these orders?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Mr. Stamp at this occasion used only some dispatches that he used to try and --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I have to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you cannot make such a conclusion on the basis of that, so that's my objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm so sorry to interrupt the objection, but the objection is not a proper one. This is a matter for cross-examination, and if he is going to object in that manner --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your question was one that was hardly supported by what had gone before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But it's a question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In those terms --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is why I wanted to give --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You might ask whether there was any change of procedure and compliance between those dates, and you could not be criticized.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is probably a better way to ask it but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Stamp, don't debate with counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Having regard to the document that you just saw and what you know, were there any changes in the procedure in respect to compliance with the orders for deployment?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: Until the 1st of May, 1999, as far as I can recall, no changes happened. This is -- this was the standard procedure to rotate units. And after that, after the 1st of May, 1999, and throughout the entire rest of the 1999, I couldn't say because I was no longer there. I was assigned to work on a different position in the Federal Ministry of the Interior in Belgrade, so don't -- can't say anything about what happened after the 1st of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could this one be tendered into evidence, Your Honours, and be given an exhibit number. I think this one is on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01200.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Keric, in order to save some time, and with the leave of the Court, of course, I want to show you a set of documents quickly, and basically I'd like you just to tell us whether or not these were orders issued by the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, or if you see anything in them which would indicate that they were not. I think you were shown all of these before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So if we could move quickly to 5301.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Orders from the ministry. These are orders from the Ministry of the Interior, public security department. This one is on the abuse of sick leave, and other issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you just look at the second page and say more precisely where in the ministry it's from?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: This is public security department. There is no signature by hand but a printed signature by the head of the RJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could this one be received in evidence and given an exhibit number, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit P01201.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we move to 5302.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a dispatch from the ministry, or rather, from the public security department, on the needs to carry out strengthened security measures in the territory of each Secretariat in order to prevent terrorist activities, explosions, burnings, arsons, and other events. It was sent to all Secretariats existing in the territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Could that one be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01202.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at 5303.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you indicate what it is quickly?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: Can you just increase the font, please. I can't see the exact date, but this document is related to the time just very close or very close before the air-strikes by NATO to increase security measures by updating defence plans, by protecting vital facilities, by protecting important people; and it's a dispatch which was sent by the ministry, by the public security department chief Vlastimir Djordjevic who signed it too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you could pause quickly on this one. Although we can't make out the date, can you make out the month and the year of the document?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: I can see that the year is 1998. I suppose it's the end, something like October -- 17th of October or the 7th of October, but I'm not sure. But it should be somewhere at the end of the year because it talks about imminent danger to the territorial integrity of the country, as it says in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The document, you will see, contains various orders.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: These are orders to prepare for carrying out measures in saving and protecting people and facilities if air-strikes occur, which did happen in that particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were the PJP command an organisational unit of the RJB?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question. Do you mean the Secretariat or some place else?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The PJP command that was sometimes the addressee?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: The PJP command was in the Ministry of the Interior in Belgrade, and the organisational structure of the command consisted of something that was called detachments and these --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, what I'm asking you is --

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: -- were located in the Secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The PJP command that you and other SUP chiefs sometimes addressed your responses to the deployment orders from General Djordjevic, were -- was that PJP command an organisational unit of the RJB?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: I think that formally the PJP command was part of the department. But in essence and in fact, the deployment and use of these resources, especially a large number of personnel and material resources, had to be dealt -- were dealt with directly by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. I think you have said that two or three times now, Mr. Keric, without my asking that. I'm really asking what the PJP command that you send your letters to an organisational unit of the RJB?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was. It was part of the RJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you see this order is also addressed to the ministry staff in Pristina, to the head?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: It was addressed to all Secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija. And there were seven such Secretariats of the interior: Pristina, Pec, Prizina [as interpreted], Prizren, Djakovica, Urosevac, and Kosovska Mitrovica. But at this time, I was not there because my job as the chief of the staff ended with the 23rd of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this document be given -- be marked for identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01203 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, could we now look at 5304.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What is this, Mr. Keric?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: It's a dispatch. Let me just see what it is about. It was signed by the chief of the department, sent to all Secretariats, to the ministry staff in Pristina, the head of the staff, to the post-secondary school of Internal Affairs director, and the secondary school of Internal Affairs. This is on the occasion of the 29th of November, which used to be a national holiday --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: -- although it is not celebrated lately. And it orders enhanced security measures to prevent unexpected activities. Enhanced security measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. I see here when you mention the addressees, it seemed that you missed RJB organisational units here "all - chief." Do you have that in your version in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: I do have it, but that's implied because all the dispatches that we discussed earlier, they all included all the chiefs. There were 33 in all in Serbia, Secretariats, including Kosovo. So in other words, to the special SPP, that's border police stations, all RJB organisational units here, all MUP staff in Pristina head, security institute, post-secondary school of Internal Affairs, and secondary school of Internal Affairs, so practically to all organisational units of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could 5304 be marked for identity, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01204 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at 5309, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What is this one quickly? Is this another dispatch?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: This dispatch is from the public security department. It deals with controls and traffic checks and checks of various goods, staples, foods, medicines, oil, because at this time there were already difficulties in supplying these goods. So this order is intended in order to prevent any abuses of -- with the transport of these goods to Kosovo and Metohija. And also increased checks of vehicles to make sure that no weapons or explosives are transported.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we just look at the last sentence or last paragraph on page 2 in both the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The ministry --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: -- and the chief of the RJB warn in this dispatch that the direct controls, additional controls, would be applied; and that authorised representatives of the Ministry of the Interior would actually conduct inspections of various check-points to make sure that these orders are being complied with. And this was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. In the English version it says: "... will visit check-points and regional Secretariats ..." Do you have the regional Secretariats in your copy?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: Well, it says regional Secretariats which is more correct because each Secretariat was actually established for a certain area or, well, we can use regional or district, the sense is the same practically.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was it -- or can you tell us briefly what was the role of the ministry headquarters, that is, the head of the RJB, in organising these inspections of the regional Secretariats and the various check-points?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: The chief of -- the head of the RJB, together with the other administrations, had full powers in these checks. He could order inspections to any administration within the ministry. He could order the certain measures which were to ensure the public and citizen security.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is 5309. I think this one, Your Honours, is on the list. And I'd ask that it be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01205.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And moving to March 1999, if we could look at 5315.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Briefly, can you tell us what this one is?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: This dispatch was sent to all Secretariats, to all administrations at the seat of the ministry, and it relates to additional enhanced measures, measures that had already been issued earlier in the dispatches as mentioned here. And this happened on the eve of the NATO air-strikes, on the 18th of February, which means a few days before the air-strikes. So they are calling for an increased level of security in keeping with the -- as compared to the measures that had been ordered earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Could 5315 be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01206.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look now at 5316. I think the B/C/S copy is very difficult to read on the screen, so with the assistance of the Usher, I can just hand him a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: 5316 is now the 12th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: This dispatch followed after the NATO air-strikes had already begun, and it orders certain enhanced measures in cooperation with the local authorities, the municipal authorities, the staffs of civilian protection, various rifle associations, and others. And it instructs everyone to enhance measures in discovering radio locators; explosive device; unexploded ordnance, because there was a lot of that; discovery of certain propaganda material, leaflets. And they also insist with the chiefs of districts, to take steps to normalise life and normal daily activities, the supplies of consumer goods, agricultural goods, and so on, in order to ensure that there was -- that they function normally. It was from the ministry of -- from the department of public security, although there is nothing in the signature portion. It also orders the controls of illegal trafficking of such goods. And I apologise, I see that there is a signature on the next page. So they are calling for enhanced measures and also cooperation between all various departments on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who is it from?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: It's from the department of public security at the Ministry of Interior, the chief of the department, Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic, but his signature does not appear, rather, there is a stamped signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could 5316 be received in evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01207.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Keric. Mr. Keric, the next five documents I propose to show to you, with the leave of the Court, are documents that were issued after or just about the time when you left the republican SUP to go to the federal SUP, but I understand that you have had an opportunity to review those documents. And I'm just going to show them to you briefly, and I would like you to tell us or not whether they appear to you, based on your experience as SUP chief, to be authentic orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at 5318.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, our objection would go to what Mr. Stamp just said. The documents that he will put to the witness now, which have been actually produced after he retired and it is quite certain that he could not have received them, and also in view of the fact that we will hear other witnesses who will be able to authenticate these documents, we consider that it is inappropriate to put these documents to this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has indicated his years of experience in the SUP and just for the purpose of authenticating them or saying whether or not they do or do not appear to be orders issued by the headquarters, his headquarters. He is capable of doing that from his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Proceed, and we will see what it is precisely that he can say, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This document dated 29th of April, 1999, I believe that you examined this document before. Can you say whether or not this appears to be an order by dispatch from the MUP headquarters, from the assistant minister General Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: Judging by the content, this was sent, in my view, from the ministry, from the chief of the department, which we can also conclude from the signature, and it relates to promotions and awards which was done every year and done regularly for those employees who actually did -- excelled in their work.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can this one be marked for identity, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01208 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Having had an opportunity to review this document over the weekend and it's there before you again, can you tell us from your experience whether that appears to be a genuine and authentic order from the MUP Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: As this was sent on the 1st of May, 1999, when I was physically already in the ministry, I could not really confirm this, especially so because we don't see the stamp of the signature, especially because this relates to police academy cadets and students of the college of internal affair, and it doesn't look familiar. I did see this document, but I really don't know when it arrived there because I was not there when it arrived. And there was no signature either, so I can't really tell by the signature itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we move to 5317.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This too was sent when I was already in another ministry, and I couldn't really speak of any of the these dispatches that were sent after 1st of May. Although it does say the Secretariat of the Interior public -- and in the signature part we see that it says public security service. I cannot speak about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, my question is this: Does it appear to you based on your experience to be an authentic dispatch from the ministry headquarters? Is there anything that you see about it that would indicate that it is not?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: The substance of this dispatch and also its form would indicate in my view that this is an authentic dispatch of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could 5317 be received in evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. We are mindful of your objection, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01209.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And could we look at 5320.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Look at the front page quickly and move on to the second page. And could you just tell us based on your examination of this document, and I know you have examined it before, whether or not this appears to you to be a genuine and authentic order issued by the MUP headquarters?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: Well, my answer is the same as earlier, to me it seems to be an authentic dispatch from the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we move to page 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here we also have the signature of the chief of the department, the assistant minister for public security, Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Could that one be received in evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01210.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, the last document in total.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have one more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I could just finish this. Could we look at 5321.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is a document demobilising MUP reservists. And, again, it's dated in August 1999 after you had left the republican MUP, but does it appear to be a genuine order from the MUP headquarters? Is there anything that gives you reason to think that it is not a genuine order?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE KERIC
utterances.text: I cannot confirm this, but judging by the style in which it was drafted, I would say that this is a genuine document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Could this one be received in evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01211.
